_notes: All values are configurable. Entries marked PLACEHOLDER are typical/assumed numbers that were NOT verified against a datasheet or measured on the board: replace them before drawing hardware conclusions.
Sensors are addressed by MUX address 0..6 (S0..S6 = O6_P1B..O7_P5B on the TestBoard_ADC124 B bank). Address 7 (S7) is the VMID reference channel.

sensor_defaults._note: SM311 = PZT-5H class (Steminc material table: d33 600 pC/N, d31 -270 pC/N, eps33T/eps0 3500 and tan delta 2.5 % at 1 kHz). thickness_mm is an ASSUMPTION: 0.25 mm taken from the SMD22T25311S disc page; replace with the real element thickness or measure Cp.

mux._note: TMUX1308A at VDD = 3.3 V, 25 C, typical column of datasheet SCDS477A (rev A, June 2025). Source of each value is listed in README.md. roff_ohm and the single-sign leakage are modelling choices, not datasheet numbers.

opamp._note: OPA365 behavioral model from datasheet SBOS365G (typ, 25 C; GBW/SR are specified at VS = 5 V, used unchanged at 3.3 V).

timing._note: Per sensor visit, from the MUX address command: all n_mux muxes switch together and share t_sensor_settle; the ADC then converts the muxes one after the other, one SPI word (adc_word_clocks clocks at adc_spi_clk_hz) each. The simulated mux is the first one: its sample is held adc_acquisition_clocks after the settle time, and it waits (n_mux - 1) words on the channel while the others are converted. Connected time per visit = settle + n_mux words (5 us with 4 muxes at 16 MHz). Then, with vmid_visit_after_each, a VMID visit of t_vmid_settle + t_vmid_park, otherwise one VMID park per sweep. ADC124S101: 16-clock word, 3 acquisition clocks.

two_pulses.description: Force pulses on sensors 2 and 4 with soft (40 us) edges, short run, with a zero-force baseline run for the delta.

baseline.description: No force. 60 ms (450 scan cycles) at the full 5 ns resolution: the baseline of every channel converges within about 5 ms (time constant ~0.5 ms), so the value is the steady state a 3 s run would also show. A brute-force 3 s run at this resolution is ~6e8 time points (~10 GB); with a coarse step the sample is dominated by solver noise (+-5 mV), see README.

baseline_vmid1ms.description: Same as baseline but with a 1 ms VMID settle (t_vmid_settle_us = 1000), 100 ms run (~14 scan cycles of ~7.1 ms), full 5 ns resolution. Each sensor is connected only 5 us per ~7.1 ms, so the bias network refreshes it far less often.
